title: The differentials of a p-basis form a basis of the Kähler differentials
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number and $K/k$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] of fields of characteristic $p$. Let $K^p=\{b^p:b\in K\}$ and let $kK^p$ be the subfield of $K$ generated by $k$ and $K^p$. Let $(t_i)_{i\in I}$ be a family of elements of $K$ such that the monomials $t^E=\prod_{i\in I}t_i^{e_i}$, where $E=(e_i)_{i\in I}$ runs over the families of integers with $0\le e_i<p$ for all $i$ and $e_i=0$ for all but finitely many $i$, form a basis of $K$ as a vector space over $kK^p$. Let $\mathrm d:K\to\Omega_{K/k}$ be the module of Kähler differentials of $K$ over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Then the family $(\mathrm dt_i)_{i\in I}$ is a basis of the $K$-vector space $\Omega_{K/k}$.

Hence we see that dx_i forms a basis for Omega_{K/k} over K'); tags verified in stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: Put B = kK^p. Induction on the intermediate-field adjunction proves that the universal k-derivation kills B, using the p-th power rule, additivity, Leibniz and the inverse rule. Induction on finitely supported monomial exponents shows that every monomial differential lies in the K-span of the dt_i. Expand a in the given B-basis and differentiate the finite sum. Therefore every da lies in this span, which is all of Omega by span_range_derivation.

proof.text: Evaluation e:B[X_i] -> K is surjective: for a in K evaluate the polynomial sum_E b.repr(a)(E) X^E. The defining equation for b and linearCombination_repr identify its value with a.

proof.text: The given monomial basis is linearly independent. Apply the partial-derivative evaluation-kernel lemma to each i. Derivation.liftOfSurjective descends the formal partial derivative along e; restrict scalars from B to k. The resulting k-derivation delta_i has delta_i(t_j) equal to the Kronecker delta, by the lift evaluation formula and pderiv_X.

proof.text: Lift each delta_i through the universal derivation to a K-linear functional on Omega. These functionals are dual to dt_i, so LinearIndependent.of_pairwise_dual_eq_zero_one proves independence. Module.Basis.mk combines independence with the span equality, and mk_apply gives the required basis values. All sums and monomials have finite support; the proof also works for empty I.

blueprint_update.statement: Let $p$ be a prime number and $K/k$ a field extension of fields of characteristic $p$. Let $K^p=\{b^p:b\in K\}$ and let $kK^p$ be the subfield of $K$ generated by $k$ and $K^p$. Let $(t_i)_{i\in I}$ be a family of elements of $K$ such that the monomials $t^E=\prod_{i\in I}t_i^{e_i}$, where $E=(e_i)_{i\in I}$ runs over the families of integers with $0\le e_i<p$ for all $i$ and $e_i=0$ for all but finitely many $i$, form a basis of $K$ as a vector space over $kK^p$. Let $\mathrm d:K\to\Omega_{K/k}$ be the module of Kähler differentials of $K$ over $k$. Then the family $(\mathrm dt_i)_{i\in I}$ is a basis of the $K$-vector space $\Omega_{K/k}$.

proof.text: (The intermediate field and its constants.) Put $B=kK^p\subseteq K$. Since $K$ has characteristic $p$, Frobenius $a\mapsto a^p$ is a field homomorphism onto the subfield $K^p$: $(a+b)^p=a^p+b^p$ and $(a^{-1})^p=(a^p)^{-1}$ for $a\ne0$. The $k$-derivation $\mathrm d_{K/k}:K\to\Omega_{K/k}$ kills $k$ by definition and kills $K^p$, since $\mathrm d(a^p)=p a^{p-1}\mathrm da=0$. Its kernel is a subfield: additivity and Leibniz give closure under sums and products, and $0=\mathrm d(1)=\mathrm d(aa^{-1})=a\mathrm d(a^{-1})+a^{-1}\mathrm da$ gives $\mathrm d(a^{-1})=-a^{-2}\mathrm da$. Therefore $\mathrm d_{K/k}$ kills every $b\in B$.

(The presentation supplied by the $p$-basis.) Form $P=B[X_i:i\in I]$ and its evaluation map $e:P\to K$, $X_i\mapsto t_i$. Let $J=(X_i^p-t_i^p:i\in I)\subseteq P$; $t_i^p\in K^p\subseteq B$, so $J\subseteq\ker e$. Every polynomial involves only finitely many variables. In $P/J$ replace each factor $X_i^{q_ip+r_i}$, $0\le r_i<p$, by $(t_i^p)^{q_i}X_i^{r_i}$; applying this to each monomial shows that the classes of $X^E=\prod_iX_i^{e_i}$ for finitely supported $0\le e_i<p$ span $P/J$ over $B$. Their images $t^E$ form a $B$-basis of $K$ by the hypothesis, so the induced $B$-linear map $P/J\to K$ is surjective and injective: any relation among the spanning classes maps to a relation among the independent $t^E$, forcing all its coefficients to be zero. Hence $\ker e=J$ and $K\cong P/J$ as $B$-algebras, with the class of $X_i$ identified with $t_i$.

(Differentials over $B$.) The module $\Omega_{P/B}$ is free over $P$ on $(\mathrm dX_i)_{i\in I}$ and $K\otimes_P\Omega_{P/B}$ is free over $K$ on $(1\otimes\mathrm dX_i)_{i\in I}$. The conormal sequence of $B\to P\to P/J\cong K$ is the exact sequence $J/J^2\xrightarrow{\delta}K\otimes_P\Omega_{P/B}\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{K/B}\to0$, where $\delta(f\bmod J^2)=1\otimes\mathrm df$ and $w(1\otimes\mathrm dX_i)=\mathrm dt_i$. For each generator $f_i=X_i^p-t_i^p$ of $J$, $\mathrm df_i=pX_i^{p-1}\mathrm dX_i-\mathrm d_B(t_i^p)=0$, because $p=0$ in $B$ and $t_i^p$ is a constant of $P/B$. For $f=\sum_{j=1}^nh_jf_{i_j}\in J$ the Leibniz rule gives $1\otimes\mathrm df=\sum_j e(h_j)\otimes\mathrm df_{i_j}+\sum_j e(f_{i_j})\otimes\mathrm dh_j=0$. Thus $\delta=0$, $w$ is an isomorphism, and $(\mathrm d_{K/B}t_i)_{i\in I}$ is a $K$-basis of $\Omega_{K/B}$..

(Return to differentials over $k$.) The first fundamental exact sequence of $k\to B\to K$ is $K\otimes_B\Omega_{B/k}\xrightarrow{u}\Omega_{K/k}\xrightarrow{v}\Omega_{K/B}\to0$, where $u(c\otimes\mathrm d_{B/k}b)=c\,\mathrm d_{K/k}b$ and $v(\mathrm d_{K/k}a)=\mathrm d_{K/B}a$. Step 1 shows $u=0$ on these generators, hence $u=0$. Exactness says $\ker v=\operatorname{im}u=0$ and $v$ is surjective, so $v$ is a $K$-linear isomorphism. It sends each $\mathrm d_{K/k}t_i$ to $\mathrm d_{K/B}t_i$, which is a basis by Step 3. Therefore $(\mathrm d_{K/k}t_i)_{i\in I}$ is a $K$-basis of $\Omega_{K/k}$, including the case $I=\emptyset$.
